front: State the ASE 2015 normal LVEF ranges for men and women.
back: Men: 52–72%. Women: 54–74%. Mildly abnormal 41–51/53%; moderately abnormal 30–40%; severely abnormal <30%.

front: State the ASE 2015 LV mass index cutoffs for LVH by 2D echo.
back: Men > 102 g/m², women > 88 g/m². (M-mode cutoffs are slightly higher: men > 115, women > 95.)

front: How is relative wall thickness (RWT) calculated, and what is the cutoff for concentric geometry?
back: RWT = 2 × PWTd / LVIDd. Concentric geometry: RWT > 0.42. Normal ~0.34.

front: Classify LV geometry using LV mass index and RWT.
back: Normal: normal mass + RWT ≤ 0.42. Concentric remodeling: normal mass + RWT > 0.42. Concentric hypertrophy: ↑ mass + RWT > 0.42. Eccentric hypertrophy: ↑ mass + RWT ≤ 0.42.

front: Match geometry to typical etiology: concentric hypertrophy vs eccentric hypertrophy vs concentric remodeling.
back: Concentric hypertrophy: pressure overload (AS, chronic HTN). Eccentric hypertrophy: volume overload (chronic AR, chronic MR). Concentric remodeling: hypertensive heart with small cavity (classically the older woman with HFpEF phenotype).

front: State the '2D wall thickness only' criteria for LV hypertrophy.
back: Normal < 1.1 cm. Mild LVH 1.1–1.2 cm. Moderate LVH 1.2–1.4 cm. Severe LVH > 1.4 cm.

front: What is the recommended 2D method for calculating LV volumes?
back: Biplane Simpson's method of disks — from A4C and A2C views. Include papillary muscles and major trabeculations INSIDE the chamber. Foreshortening is the main pitfall.

front: How do 2D-derived LV volumes typically compare with cMRI-derived volumes? And EF?
back: 2D underestimates volumes compared to cMRI (foreshortening + geometric assumptions). Contrast echo and 3D echo are closer. EF is similar across all modalities.

front: State the two-part LV mass formula from linear measurements.
back: LV mass (g) = 0.8 × [1.04 × ((LVIDd + PWTd + IVSd)³ − LVIDd³)] + 0.6. Concept: volume of thick-walled ellipsoid minus inner chamber volume, × specific gravity of muscle.

front: State Laplace's law for LV wall stress and its implications.
back: Wall stress = (LV pressure × chamber radius) / (2 × wall thickness). Hypertrophy minimizes wall stress. Pressure overload → ↑ thickness. Volume overload → ↑ radius (with proportional wall growth = eccentric hypertrophy).

front: Formula for stroke volume by Doppler at any site?
back: SV (mL) = CSA (cm²) × VTI (cm). Common sites: LVOT (CSA_LVOT × VTI_LVOT), mitral annulus (CSA × VTI_inflow), RVOT for right-heart SV.

front: Formula for fractional shortening and its normal range?
back: FS = (LVIDd − LVIDs) / LVIDd × 100. Normal 25–45%. Unreliable when regional wall-motion abnormalities are present.

front: Why is midwall FS a better marker of contractility than endocardial FS in concentric hypertrophy?
back: Midwall FS captures BOTH inward endocardial motion AND wall thickening. In concentric hypertrophy, endocardial FS overestimates function because the thickened wall generates inward endocardial excursion that isn't matched by true contractility.

front: State the dP/dt formula from the MR CW jet and its normal range.
back: dP/dt (mmHg/s) = 32 / Δt (s), where Δt is the time to travel from 1 m/s to 3 m/s on the MR envelope. Normal ≥ 1200 mmHg/s; abnormal < 1000 mmHg/s.

front: State the myocardial performance (Tei) index formula and normal values.
back: MPI = (IVCT + IVRT) / ET. Normal LV Tei < 0.4. RV Tei: < 0.43 by PW, < 0.54 by TDI.

front: Grade the four levels of wall motion in a 4-point scoring system.
back: 1 = normal/hyperkinetic. 2 = hypokinetic (< 50% thickening or < 5 mm excursion). 3 = akinetic (no thickening). 4 = dyskinetic (systolic thinning or paradoxical outward motion). Wall Motion Score Index = sum / segments; normal = 1.

front: Which coronary artery supplies each LV wall in the 17-segment model?
back: LAD: entire septum, anterior wall, anterior half of apex. RCA (right-dominant): basal-mid inferior and inferoseptal walls. LCx: basal and mid lateral wall. Apex has overlap (all three).

front: What is a normal peak global longitudinal strain (GLS)?
back: Approximately −20% (more negative = more strain). Values less negative than −18% are abnormal. Note: strain is expressed as a negative number by convention.

front: What relative reduction in GLS during chemotherapy suggests subclinical cardiotoxicity?
back: A relative reduction > 15% compared to baseline GLS. Detects dysfunction before EF falls.

front: Describe the classic strain pattern of cardiac amyloid.
back: Apical sparing of longitudinal strain with reduced basal and mid strain — the 'cherry-on-top' bullseye pattern.

front: Which parameter of systolic function is essentially load-independent?
back: End-systolic volume (ESV). EF, strain, MPI/Tei, and dP/dt all remain load-dependent to varying degrees. Strain rate is a reasonable analogue for contractility.

front: State the ASE 2015 upper limit for LVEDVi in men and women.
back: Men: 74 mL/m². Women: 61 mL/m².

front: What is the End-systolic volume (ESVi) prognostic threshold for post-MI mortality?
back: ESV < 95 mL after MI: ~10% 5-year mortality. Larger ESV predicts higher mortality (30% for markedly dilated ventricles).

front: How does exercise typically change EDV, ESV, and EF in a normal heart?
back: EDV unchanged or slightly decreased. EF increases. ESV decreases (more complete emptying, higher contractility with catecholamines).

front: What is the M-mode measurement convention for LV chamber dimensions?
back: Leading-edge to leading-edge. In 2D, use inner-edge to inner-edge (white-black interface). M-mode values are typically slightly larger than 2D values.

front: What is pulsus alternans and what does it signify on echo?
back: Beat-to-beat variation in the systolic velocity or stroke volume with alternating strong and weak beats — a marker of severely impaired myocardial function.

front: Why does the RV normally have a lower EF than the LV even though right- and left-sided stroke volumes match?
back: Right heart EDV is larger than left heart EDV. Because SV/EDV = EF, the same stroke volume comes from a larger baseline volume, giving a lower EF (typically ≥ 45% is normal for RV).

front: Why must LV volumes be measured with the true apex included?
back: Foreshortening — imaging that cuts off the apex — underestimates LV length and volume. Use extended focus, off-axis views, or 3D to avoid it. It is the single biggest source of TTE volume underestimation vs cMRI.
